name: Times club monthly special crossword No 20,246

solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Forced to hide a month abroad she wouldn’t be “missed”

indicators.note: to hide something is to keep it out of sight inside, so the forced word wraps round what follows

blocks.note: made someone do it means forced them to
taken as written
M is the standard abbreviation for month

explanation.surface: Someone is compelled to conceal a month spent overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: Missed in quotes is the trick: a woman abroad is addressed not as Miss but by the French married title.
explanation.definitionFit: In France a married woman is addressed as Madame rather than Mademoiselle, the French counterpart of Miss.

clue.text: Gracious man’s act of self-harm, one roughly involving initiation in rites?

blocks.note: my! and gracious! are both exclamations of surprise
a stag is a man on his own, as at a stag party
an own goal (OG) is a footballer harming his own side
the Roman numeral for one
c, circa, means roughly or about

explanation.surface: A kindly man somehow hurts himself during an initiation ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: MY + STAG + OG + I + C gives MYSTAGOGIC; OG for own goal is a common crossword abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A mystagogue leads novices into religious mysteries, so the adjective describes teaching that admits people to secret ceremonies.

clue.text: Party, one often accompanying ER at opening of annual parliament

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its very start, so only its first letter is wanted

blocks.note: a do is a party or social event
um and er are hesitation sounds heard together in halting speech
the first letter of annual

explanation.surface: A celebration with the Queen present marks the annual State Opening of Parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: ER looks like Elizabeth Regina at the State Opening, but here it is the hesitation er, which um so often accompanies.
explanation.definitionFit: The douma (usually Duma) is the elected Russian legislative assembly, first convened under the Tsar.

clue.text: Dutch title of hymn rendered poetically always

indicators.note: a piece rendered by a performer is given a new version, so these letters come out rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, ready to be rearranged
e'er is the poetic contraction of ever, meaning always

explanation.surface: The heading of a hymn translated into Dutch verse for all time.
explanation.definitionFit: Mynheer is the Dutch form of address equivalent to Sir or Mister, used formerly of Dutchmen in English.

clue.text: University visits drop off, according to champion of old poetry

indicators.note: whoever visits goes inside a place, so the university letter goes into the next word

blocks.note: to drop off is to doze, fall into light sleep
U is the usual abbreviation for university
per means according to, as in per the rules

explanation.surface: A student's lecture visits make them nod off, by one account.
explanation.definitionFit: The douzepers were the twelve peers or paladins of Charlemagne, heroic champions celebrated in medieval romance verse.

clue.text: See rising mould, and film that’s well established?

indicators.note: in a down clue something rising is read from bottom to top, so the word is turned round

blocks.note: lo! is an old word for look or see
a die is a mould for shaping metal

explanation.surface: Watch mould grow and a film form, an old and familiar process.
explanation.walkthrough: Mould and film look like fungal growth; mould is a die and film is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An oldie is anything old and familiar, such as a classic movie that has been around for decades.

clue.text: Turning up never-endingly in attic, coppers and flutes

indicators.note: never-endingly means each word is denied its final letter
turning up in a down clue means reading upwards, so the string runs backwards

blocks.note: taken as written, to lose its last letter
a loft is an attic, to lose its last letter
the fuzz is slang for the police, to lose its last letter

explanation.surface: Police and some musical instruments turn up in a loft.
explanation.walkthrough: Shorn of last letters, IN, LOFT and FUZZ become I LOF FUZ, which reads upwards as ZUFFOLI.
explanation.definitionFit: Zuffoli are small Italian flageolets or whistle pipes, the plural of zufolo, so they are a kind of flute.

clue.text: Fire devotee for ultimately petty breaches in due course

indicators.note: ultimately points to the last letter of the word it qualifies
to breach a wall is to break into it, so that letter goes inside the word for

blocks.note: pro means in favour of, for
the last letter of petty
later means eventually, in due course

explanation.surface: Minor offences against fire regulations will be dealt with in time.
explanation.definitionFit: A pyrolater is a fire-worshipper, from Greek pyr (fire) and latreia (worship).

clue.text: Revive, dismissing one who may send off letter from the ME

indicators.note: to dismiss someone is to send them away, so those letters leave the word

blocks.note: to refresh is to revive
a referee can send a player off the pitch

explanation.surface: Revive a footballer after the official who sends players off is removed.
explanation.walkthrough: REFRESH loses REF to leave RESH; ME is the Middle East, not me.
explanation.definitionFit: Resh is the twentieth letter of the Hebrew alphabet, Hebrew being a language of the Middle East.

clue.text: Writing poorly, perceiving abnormally upsetting stammer

indicators.note: upsetting things abnormally knocks them out of their normal order

blocks.note: to misspell is to write words wrongly

explanation.surface: Bad handwriting and strange perception can upset someone who stammers.
explanation.walkthrough: MISSPELL, the verb behind writing poorly, is rearranged into PSELLISM.
explanation.definitionFit: Psellism is a medical term for a speech defect such as stuttering, from Greek psellos, faltering.

clue.text: Cut dead old ends off, having turned up something that smells

definitions.text: having turned up something that smells
definitions.note: describes a nose turned up at the tip

indicators.note: off means gone bad or awry, so these letters are not in their proper order

blocks.note: to cut someone dead is to snub them
O is the abbreviation for old
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone ignores an old acquaintance after sniffing out something smelly.
explanation.walkthrough: SNUB is followed by O and ENDS rearranged into NOSED.
explanation.definitionFit: A snub nose is short and tilted upward at the tip, so the adjective describes a face with an upturned nose.

clue.text: What finishes off army for good — plus old militias

indicators.note: what finishes each word is its final letter, so only the closing letters are taken

blocks.note: the last letters of off, army, for, good and plus

explanation.surface: Something ends a soldier's army career permanently, along with old reserve forces.
explanation.definitionFit: The fyrd was the Anglo-Saxon local levy of free men called up for military service, so the plural is ancient militias.

clue.text: A handle shielded from the wind material exposed to the elements

blocks.note: taken as written
a handle is a name or label for someone
the lee is the side sheltered from the wind
toile is a linen or cotton fabric

explanation.surface: A grip sheltered from the wind is made of fabric left out in the weather.
explanation.walkthrough: Handle seems to be a grip but is a name, giving LABEL.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase à la belle étoile means under the stars, sleeping in the open air without shelter.

clue.text: Sibling emperor putting down European with a piece of his mind?

indicators.note: putting something down shifts it lower, which in a down clue means further along the word

blocks.note: bro is short for brother
Caesar was the title of Roman emperors
E is the abbreviation for European
taken as written

explanation.surface: A brother emperor overrules a European while giving him a piece of his mind.
explanation.walkthrough: The E of CAESAR moves down to the end, giving CASARE, then A follows. Giving someone a piece of your mind is an idiom for scolding.
explanation.definitionFit: Broca's area is a region of the brain's frontal lobe governing speech production, literally a part of anyone's mind.

clue.text: Old runner’s major slip: not the first

indicators.note: not the first means the opening letter is left off

blocks.note: a howler is a glaring blunder

explanation.surface: A veteran athlete made a big mistake and did not finish first.
explanation.walkthrough: Runner is not an athlete but a smuggler, someone who runs contraband.
explanation.definitionFit: An owler was a smuggler, especially of wool or sheep out of England, working by night like an owl.

clue.text: Landlords at first start losing it when housing bill slashed

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of the word before
losing something means it drops out of the word
housing means holding inside, so the bill goes within the letters before it

blocks.note: the first letter of landlords
to initiate is to start
taken as written, the letters removed
ac, account, is a bill

explanation.surface: Landlords begin to lose out once a bill is cut.
explanation.walkthrough: The bill goes in straight after the landlords' initial, so the container wraps the first piece and the shortened start together.
explanation.definitionFit: In botany laciniate leaves or petals are deeply cut into narrow irregular lobes, looking jagged or slit.

clue.text: Dealer out of dope, briefly left in charge, turned corrupt

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the word loses its last letter
turned means turned round, so the word reads back to front

blocks.note: dope is slang for information
L is the abbreviation for left
IC stands for in charge
to rot is to decay or corrupt

explanation.surface: A drug dealer runs out of supply and is put in charge, then goes bad.
explanation.walkthrough: Dealer and dope suggest drugs; but dope is information and dealer out is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An inflictor deals out blows or punishment, imposing something unpleasant on others.

clue.text: Fathom being, primarily, both slack and firm on the inside? It’s a teaser

indicators.note: on the inside means placed within, so these go inside the fathom abbreviation
primarily means firstly, so the opening letter is taken

blocks.note: fm is the abbreviation for fathom
lax means slack or loose
Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm
the first letter of being

explanation.surface: Understanding a person who is both loose and firm inside is quite a puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: Teaser looks like a puzzle but means something that teases fibres apart.
explanation.definitionFit: A flax-comb, or hackle, is a toothed tool that combs out and separates flax fibres, which is what teasing fibres means.

clue.text: Ache one aims to shift restricted blood flow

indicators.note: to shift things is to move them around, so the letters are reordered

blocks.note: taken as written
the Roman numeral for one
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sufferer hopes to ease a pain caused by poor circulation.
explanation.definitionFit: Ischaemia is an inadequate supply of blood to a part of the body, caused by narrowed or blocked arteries.

clue.text: Some personal ad is passed over, being in a niche area?

indicators.note: some of the following words means only part of their run of letters is used
over in a down clue suggests turning upside down, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: the letters spanning the end of personal through the start of passed

explanation.surface: A lonely-hearts advert is ignored, being aimed at a narrow audience.
explanation.walkthrough: Niche area looks like a specialist market, but an apse is a literal recess in a church.
explanation.definitionFit: Apsidal describes something shaped like or belonging to an apse, the vaulted semicircular recess at the end of a church.

clue.text: A home for gnomes concealing case of gold

indicators.note: concealing its case means the outer letters are hidden away, leaving only the inside

blocks.note: taken as written
the gnomes of Zurich is a nickname for Swiss bankers

explanation.surface: A garden gnome's house hides a box of gold.
explanation.walkthrough: Gnomes suggests garden ornaments, but the gnomes of Zurich are Swiss financiers; ZURICH without its outer letters is URIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Auric is the chemistry adjective for gold, from Latin aurum, especially gold in its trivalent state.

clue.text: No longer making up any gibe when rattled

indicators.note: something rattled is shaken about, so the letters are mixed up

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A person stops apologising whenever a taunt gets under their skin.
explanation.definitionFit: To abye was an archaic verb meaning to pay the penalty for or atone, so abyeing is obsolete for making amends.

clue.text: With toes like birds’, can’t I do as bats, and mean to push last forward?

indicators.note: bats means crazy, so the letters go wild
pushing the last letter forward moves the final letter to the front

blocks.note: taken as written, ignoring the apostrophe
lousy means mean or stingy

explanation.surface: Someone envies birds' feet, unable to hang upside down like bats.
explanation.walkthrough: Bats looks like the animals but is the anagram signal; LOUSY with its Y moved to the front becomes YLOUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Anisodactylous feet have three toes forward and one back, unequal digits, the arrangement found in perching birds.

clue.text: Forgotten deck, the lower one of two maybe now hotel

indicators.note: now marks what stands in that position from here on, replacing what was there

blocks.note: two is an example of a digit
in a down entry the lower of the two I letters is the second
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A forgotten pack of cards, the bottom one perhaps a two, now in a hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: Deck seems to be cards, but it is the verb to adorn; one is the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Dight is an archaic verb meaning to dress or adorn, which is the decorating sense of deck.

clue.text: Anything that’s revolting found in books

indicators.note: found in means sitting inside, so the disgusted word goes inside the books

blocks.note: OT, the Old Testament, is a collection of books
ugh! is what one says at something revolting

explanation.surface: Anything disgusting turns up in books.
explanation.definitionFit: Ought is an old variant spelling of aught, meaning anything at all, as in for aught I know.

clue.text: Homeless child has question for one endowing property

indicators.note: for one means in place of one, so the Roman one gives way to the question letter

blocks.note: a waif is a homeless, neglected child
Q is the abbreviation for question

explanation.surface: A street child asks a question of a property benefactor.
explanation.walkthrough: WAIF has its I (one) replaced by Q.
explanation.definitionFit: Under Islamic law a waqf is a charitable endowment, property given in perpetuity for religious or public use.

clue.text: Once ashore, trailer loaded with large article

indicators.note: a vehicle loaded with cargo carries it inside

blocks.note: a film trailer is an advertisement, an ad
L is the abbreviation for large
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A vehicle's trailer carries a big item from a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: Trailer looks like something towed, but a cinema trailer is an AD, which holds L and AN: A(L AN)D.
explanation.definitionFit: Aland is an archaic adverb meaning on land or to the shore, as opposed to at sea.

clue.text: Set on backing fancier NZ fieldworker

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the word is read in reverse

blocks.note: to set upon or attack someone in the street is to mug them
to dig something is to fancy it, so a fancier is a digger

explanation.surface: Someone attacked a pigeon fancier who works the fields of New Zealand.
explanation.walkthrough: Set on is an attack, MUG, reversed to GUM; dig as slang for like makes a fancier a DIGGER.
explanation.definitionFit: Gum-diggers dug up fossilised kauri resin from the fields and swamps of northern New Zealand.

clue.text: Rarely paid much for filling up cattle enclosures

blocks.note: feed is a rare past tense of fee, to pay a fee to
lots means much, a great deal

explanation.surface: Seldom paying much for fodder to fill a herd's pens.
explanation.walkthrough: Rarely marks a rare word form, not frequency.
explanation.definitionFit: Feedlots are enclosures where livestock are fattened intensively on grain before slaughter, hence they fill cattle up.

clue.text: Assembly’s voice on reflection with some weight earlier

indicators.note: a reflection in a mirror is reversed, so the word reads backwards

blocks.note: kg, kilogram, is a weight
alto is a singing voice

explanation.surface: An assembly's spokesperson, looking back, carries some weight from before.
explanation.definitionFit: A kgotla is a traditional public meeting or community council in Botswana, presided over by the chief.
